title: "6.8 Monitoring plan"
order: 8

## What is monitored

A tool does not drift the way a model does: the same inputs always give the same output.
What moves is the inputs — the book, the PD the scorecard gives it, and the market
assumptions — and with them what the tool reports. The plan therefore watches three things:
**the book's position against the hurdle**, **where the mispricing sits**, and **every change
to an input the tool does not compute itself**. The thresholds are policy constants
(`wiki/facts/policy.py`), printed here by name; "points" are percentage points of the book.

| Metric | Population | Threshold | Frequency | Action on breach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Share clearing the hurdle at the quoted rate | the booked book, and each new cohort of bookings | moving by more than {{< var monitoring.pricing_share_move >}} points from development | every pricing run | Find the input that moved, in this order: `MARKET`, the scorecard (a retrain or recalibration), the mix of new bookings. Report to the pricing tool owner. |
| Below-break-even share and EAD | the same | the share moving by more than {{< var monitoring.pricing_share_move >}} points from development; any rise in a cohort of new bookings | every pricing run | Report to the pricing committee as loss-making business, by band (finding 2). |
| Mispriced share and mispriced EAD, by score band | the same | a band's share moving by more than {{< var monitoring.pricing_share_move >}} points from development | every pricing run | Read beside D4's band calibration on the booked (finding 3): a move in the bands the PD under-predicts is checked against the PD before the price. |
| Median ROE at the quoted rate | the same | reported, not thresholded | every pricing run | Read against the hurdle and the share clearing. |
| Market assumptions | `shared.config.MARKET` | any change to any value | every change | Owner's sign-off, a dated entry in the change log, then re-run 6.5, 6.6 and D8's gate before the value is used (finding 5). |
| The PD's calibration by band | booked loans with outcomes (D4's check) | D4's tolerance, {{< var monitoring.ratio_lo >}} to {{< var monitoring.ratio_hi >}}, on at least {{< var monitoring.min_band_defaults >}} defaults | when outcomes mature | A breach in D4 is a pricing event too: re-run pricing after the recalibration (finding 3). |
| Arithmetic identities and what-if equals batch | every booked loan | any residual at or above {{< var pricing.test_tolerance >}}; any verdict flip | every `verify.py` run and every test run | The build fails. Fix the cause in the code; never loosen the check ([6.9](gate.qmd)). |
| Book summary against the committed summary | the booked book | relative drift above {{< var pricing.verify_tolerance >}} in `n`, `share_clears` or `mispriced_ead` | every `verify.py` run | `verify.py` fails: the data, the scorecard or `MARKET` changed. Rebuild the priced book deliberately, or restore the checkpoint ([6.9](gate.qmd)). |

The share rows are the control for findings 2 and 3 and the context for finding 1: a move in
the share clearing is read against the inputs that can cause it, never as a change in pricing
discipline while the quotes are generated. The {{< var monitoring.pricing_share_move >}}-point
threshold is smaller than the swing of a {{< var pricing.sens.step >}} move in the cost of
funds ([6.6](sensitivity.qmd)) and larger than that of the same move in the operating cost or
tax rate: a change in the dominant assumption always shows, and a small one in a minor
assumption does not raise a false alarm.

## Development baselines {#pr-development-baselines}

What "no change" looks like, measured at development on the booked book.

| Metric | Development value | Population |
|---|---|---|
| Share clearing the hurdle | {{< var pricing.share_clears >}} ({{< var pricing.n_clears >}} loans) | booked book, {{< var pricing.n >}} loans |
| Mispriced EAD | \${{< var pricing.mispriced_ead >}} ({{< var pricing.mispriced_ead_share >}} of EAD) | booked book |
| Below break-even | {{< var pricing.below_break_even.share >}} ({{< var pricing.below_break_even.n >}} loans, \${{< var pricing.below_break_even.ead >}}) | booked book |
| Median ROE at the quoted rate | {{< var pricing.median_roe >}} | booked book |
| Median quoted / recommended rate | {{< var pricing.median_quoted_rate >}} / {{< var pricing.median_recommended_rate >}} | booked book |

| Score band | Mispriced share | Mispriced EAD ($) | Population |
|---|---|---|---|
| D | {{< var pricing.band.D.mispriced_rate >}} | {{< var pricing.band.D.mispriced_ead >}} | booked book, band D |
| C | {{< var pricing.band.C.mispriced_rate >}} | {{< var pricing.band.C.mispriced_ead >}} | booked book, band C |
| B | {{< var pricing.band.B.mispriced_rate >}} | {{< var pricing.band.B.mispriced_ead >}} | booked book, band B |
| A | {{< var pricing.band.A.mispriced_rate >}} | {{< var pricing.band.A.mispriced_ead >}} | booked book, band A |
| AAA | {{< var pricing.band.AAA.mispriced_rate >}} | {{< var pricing.band.AAA.mispriced_ead >}} | booked book, band AAA |

The market assumptions at development are the table in [6.4](assumptions.qmd#pr-market);
they are the first entry of the change log finding 5 asks for.

## Events that trigger a re-run and review

Pricing is not redeveloped; it is re-run. Any one of these re-runs the pricing of the book,
re-reads [6.5](performance.qmd) and [6.6](sensitivity.qmd), and informs the validator:

1. Any change to a value in `MARKET`, or to `fee_rate`'s use.
2. Any change to the scorecard: a retrain, a recalibration, a new band boundary — every rate
   moves with the PD ([D3](../d3-dependencies.qmd#what-a-scorecard-change-forces)).
3. Any change to `pricing/src/`: the engine or the book-level functions.
4. A share threshold above breached on two consecutive pricing runs with no input change to
   explain it.

The open findings of [6.7](limitations.qmd) are acted on at the first of these that touches
them: finding 3 at D4's recalibration, findings 2 and 4 at the next change to `pricing/`,
finding 5 before the next change to `MARKET`.

## What is automated today

This plan is documented, not yet automated. The platform has one booked book and one set of
quotes, so there is no new cohort to compare. What runs today is the development side, on
every `python verify.py`: the summary comparison and the facts — every figure on these pages,
the identities and the what-if check included — recomputed through the engine from the
committed data, scorecard and `MARKET` ([6.9](gate.qmd), [D9](../d9-implementation.qmd)). A
change to `MARKET` is caught there today, because the facts recomputed from it no longer match
the committed ones; nothing yet asks for the owner's sign-off.
